Maya (eng-infra): FYI — seeing intermittent 0 endpoints on a headless svc in us-west-2-edge: `gpu-infer-edge`. Pods are Running+Ready tho.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Do you mean `kubectl get endpoints` shows empty? Or EndpointSlice exists but with 0 addresses?
Maya (eng-infra): EndpointSlice present but `addresses: []`. Example: ```kubectl get endpointslices -n infer -l kubernetes.io/service-name=gpu-infer-edge -o yaml
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
items:
- metadata:
    name: gpu-infer-edge-abc-123
  endpoints: []
  ports:
  - name: grpc
    port: 8500
```
Maya (eng-infra): Meanwhile `kubectl get pods -n infer -l app=gpu-infer -o wide` shows 3 pods on node pool with GPUs and they have Ready=true.
Sara (eng-sre): Any recent kube-proxy restarts on those nodes? We had a probe flapping bug last week where iptables restore happened after EndpointSlice controller ran.
Maya (eng-infra): I checked `journalctl -u kube-proxy -n 200` on one node, saw a restart around the same minute as the first 0-endpoint event: `Started kube-proxy.`
Dmitri (eng-platform): Could also be conntrack/masq rules being cleared when our on-prem NAT gateway healthcheck cycles. Edge nodes hit a short egress outage and we saw iptables-restore jobs triggered by our daemonset.
Kevin (eng-runtime): If kube-proxy restarts and misses ipset/iptables ordering, kube-controller might briefly register empty slices. Are pods backing with hostNetwork? (we use hostNetwork=false for these)
Maya (eng-infra): pods are normal (non-hostNetwork). Noticed `kube-controller-manager` logs complaining about stale endpoints reconciliation: `Event: EndpointsReconciler - removed stale endpoints for service/gpu-infer-edge` around same time.
Sara (eng-sre): Can you paste the `kubectl describe svc gpu-infer-edge -n infer`? Also check if EndpointSlice controller logs show errors.
Maya (eng-infra): pasted snippet: ```Name: gpu-infer-edge
Type: ClusterIP (Headless)
IP: <none> (headless)
Endpoints: <none>```
Maya (eng-infra): Also saw a warning in node kubelet: `Failed to update status: etcdserver: request timed out` — brief control-plane lag.
Dmitri (eng-platform): Sounds like a race: control-plane lag + kube-proxy restart -> EndpointSlice controller does reconciliation and writes empty endpoints because it couldn't query node/pod status timely. When things recovered, slices updated back with addresses.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Repro idea: force kube-proxy restart on one node during a simulated etcd/adb blip and see if EndpointSlice temporarily shrinks to zero. If yes we can harden by delaying reconcilers or adding a backoff.
Sara (eng-sre): Short-term mitigation: add a retry/fallback in our host routing — make the service clients tolerate transient 503s and retry with exponential backoff for ~10s. Also bump monitoring alert to suppress noisy alerts when slices == 0 for <30s.
Maya (eng-infra): Agreed. I'll add a metric-based suppression and a ticket to test forced-restart repro.
Dmitri (eng-platform): Longer term: change kube-proxy restart ordering so iptables rules are restored only after endpoint reconciliation completes, or make EndpointSlice controller more resilient to transient control-plane unavailability. Filing infra task.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Also check if `kube-proxy --cleanup-iptables-on-exit` is true in our config; if false, restarts may leave rules inconsistent.
Maya (eng-infra): Thanks. I'll schedule the repro & add a runbook snippet. cc @deploy-bot for followup job. :eyes:
deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1427: reproduce headless svc empty endpoints on kube-proxy restart, assigned to Maya. :white_check_mark:
Sara (eng-sre): Nice. If anyone hits a live incident, hit me in #eng-sre and I'll coordinate mitigation. :handshake:
